docs: The substrate: tensors, cells, colors, images, resampling, seeded chance and the canonical names.
The road from a grid of bytes to pixels, and the one JSON object every mrly thing is named by.
- `tensor` makes and tallies the byte grids; `cell` dresses one in colors and tags.
- `colors` holds the rgba color, the two themes and the house palette; `paint` spreads a palette over a cell.
- `ramp` turns counter values into colors; `resample` rescales pixels and squashes them for hex.
- `image` holds the rgba pixels a renderer returns; encoding them into a file is the caller's.
- `rng` deals seeded chance: one xoshiro256++ stream, passed by hand, never global.
- `error` holds the one error, its Result and the json parser.
- `name` holds the `Named` trait, the `kind!` marker, the text views and the sha256 a name's id is cut from; `named_enum!` names an enum.
The json value and map are serde_json's, kept under `preserve_order` so an object comes back in the order it was written and both bridges print the same text.
The doors: `Tensor::of`, `Tensor::rot90`, `Color::from_hex`, `Color::to_hex`, `Image::scale` and `ramp::color`.
The cell grid: type bytes with optional per-cell colors and tags.
The rgba color, its themes and the fifteen-color palette.
The one error type, its Result and the json parser over the rented value.
The image a renderer returns: its size and its rgba pixels.
The canonical names: one JSON object per thing, its views and its id.
The sha256 digest the ids are cut from.
The editions that distribute a palette over a cell.
The colorizers that turn counter values into colors.
The pixel resamplers and the hex squash.
The seeded random stream.
The tensor and its dtypes.

functions.name: longest
docs: Returns the index of the longest of `names` that `text` starts with, and the rest of `text`, or `None` when none matches.
A prefix reader takes the longest match, not the first, so `evens` never cuts `evens_zeros` short.
let names = vec!["evens".to_string(), "evens_zeros".to_string()];
assert_eq!(mrly_core::name::longest("evens_zeros_ones", &names), Some((1, "_ones")));
assert_eq!(mrly_core::name::longest("odds", &names), None);

assert_eq!(a.rot90(1, (0, 1)).unwrap().bytes().unwrap(), &[2, 4, 1, 3]);
assert!(a.rot90(1, (0, 2)).is_err());

functions.name: set
docs: Writes the byte at a multi-index.
# Errors
Errs when the index misses the shape or the tensor is wider than one byte.

functions.name: size
docs: Returns the number of elements.

functions.name: slice
docs: Drops one axis by fixing it at an index.
# Errors
Errs when the axis is past the rank or the index is past the axis.
let block = mrly_core::tensor::Tensor::full(vec![2, 3, 4], 1);
assert_eq!(block.slice(2, 0).unwrap(), mrly_core::tensor::Tensor::full(vec![2, 3], 1));

functions.name: sum
docs: Returns the sum of all elements.

functions.name: tile
docs: Repeats the tensor the given number of times along each axis.
# Errors
Errs without one count per axis.

functions.name: transpose
docs: Swaps two axes.
# Errors
Errs when either axis is past the rank.

functions.name: typed
docs: Builds a zeroed tensor of the shape and width.

functions.name: u16
docs: Wraps a u16 vector as a tensor of the shape.
# Errors
Errs when the data length is not the shape's product.
use mrly_core::tensor::{Dtype, Tensor};
let t = Tensor::u16(vec![1, 2, 3, 4], vec![2, 2]).unwrap();
assert_eq!((t.dtype(), t.sum()), (Dtype::U16, 10));
assert!(Tensor::u16(vec![1, 2, 3], vec![2, 2]).is_err());
